image_description: A close-up view of a sea lion resting on a rocky surface. The animal is curled up, with its head tucked towards its body. Visible features include dark brown, coarse fur, a visible external ear flap, and one foreflipper tucked near the chest. The lighting highlights the texture of the fur and the smooth skin of the flipper.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is turned away and partially obscured by the body angle; the sagittal crest is not visible from this perspective.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, small external ear flap is clearly visible on the side of the head, confirming it is an otariid (sea lion/fur seal) and not a true seal.
The snout area is facing away from the camera or obscured by shadow/fur, making whisker visibility impossible to verify.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One foreflipper is visible tucked under the body. It appears broad and the visible skin surface is dark and relatively hairless compared to the body fur, consistent with anatomy.

The asymmetrical curled posture prevents a direct visual assessment of bilateral symmetry in this specific frame.
